# Agentic Rules Catalog

> A curated, rated catalog of rules, skills, workflows, hooks, subagents, MCP servers, and plugins for coding agents, focused on Claude Code and Codex. Every entry records where it came from, its license, tags, and a curator rating.

Full metadata for every entry is in [catalog/index.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/catalog/index.json). Install steps by entry type are in the [install guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/skills/agentic-catalog/references/install.md). Repository: https://github.com/ban-red/agentic-rules

Score (1-5) = (2 × usefulness + quality + portability + novelty) / 5, where novelty means value beyond host built-ins. Evidence, from weakest to strongest: reviewed, used, tested, evaluated. Hosts: `any` means portable through an open format. Entries are ranked by score within each section. Show users the score, the evidence level, and the source before installing anything.

## Skills

- [Diagnosing bugs with a tight feedback loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md): A six-phase loop for hard bugs. Build a fast, deterministic command that goes red on this exact bug, minimise the repro, rank falsifiable hypotheses, instrument with tagged logs, fix behind a regression test at a real seam, and clean up. Includes secret redaction and a performance branch. Use when: Hard, flaky, or performance bugs where the cause is not obvious and guessing has already failed. — id `diagnosing-bugs`, score 4.8, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags debugging, feedback-loop, reproduction, performance, regression, vendored from https://github.com/mattpocock/skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/diagnosing-bugs/entry.yaml)
- [Write and prune AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/agents-md-authoring/SKILL.md): An on-demand guide for creating or auditing AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. It says what to include and exclude, how to structure nested and path-scoped files, and gives an approval-gated audit procedure that removes lines which do not change behavior. Use when: Creating project instructions, or when they have grown long or the agent ignores them. — id `agents-md-authoring`, score 4.4, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags project-instructions, agents-md, context-hygiene, monorepo, adapted from https://agents.md/, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/agents-md-authoring/entry.yaml)
- [Verification before completion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/verification-before-completion/SKILL.md): A gate before any claim that work is done, fixed, or passing. Name the command that proves the claim, run it fresh, read the output, and only then report, with a table of claims and the evidence each one needs. Use when: Agents claim success, commit, or open PRs without running the checks that prove it, or trust subagent reports without checking the diff. — id `verification-before-completion`, score 4.4, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags verification, evidence, completion-claims, testing, subagents, vendored from https://github.com/obra/superpowers, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/verification-before-completion/entry.yaml)
- [Grilling (design-tree interview)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/grilling/SKILL.md): Stress-test a plan by interviewing the user in rounds over a design tree. Each round asks every question that can be answered now, each with a recommended answer. The agent looks up facts itself, and nothing is acted on until shared understanding is confirmed. Use when: Before building something ambiguous, when you want the agent to surface every open decision instead of silently assuming. — id `grilling`, score 4.2, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags requirements, planning, interviewing, design-review, vendored from https://github.com/mattpocock/skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/grilling/entry.yaml)
- [React and Next.js performance practices (Vercel)](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/tree/dc8367e6f91c022d83361f03c3313fa05e848ee5/skills/react-best-practices): A prioritized set of about 70 React and Next.js performance rules covering request waterfalls, bundle size, server and client boundaries, re-renders, and JavaScript micro-optimizations. SKILL.md is the index, and each rule loads on demand. Use when: Writing, reviewing, or refactoring React or Next.js code where performance matters. — id `react-best-practices`, score 4.2, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags react, nextjs, performance, frontend, code-review, linked from https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/react-best-practices/entry.yaml)
- [Retrospective to durable project guidance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/retrospective/SKILL.md): After finished work, turn what slowed the session down into instructions, skills, scripts, or checks, each placed where a future session will actually load or run it, and verify that new skills trigger. Use when: You want a self-improvement loop where an agent learns from a session and writes the lessons back into the project. — id `retrospective`, score 4.0, evidence tested, hosts any, tags self-improvement, retrospective, project-instructions, skill-triggering, memory, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/retrospective/entry.yaml)
- [Fix failing GitHub Actions checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/gh-fix-ci/SKILL.md): Use gh to find failing PR checks, pull the Actions logs, and summarize the failure. Draft a fix plan, implement it only after explicit approval, and recheck. A bundled script handles changes in gh output fields and fallbacks for job logs. Use when: A pull request's GitHub Actions checks are failing and you want them diagnosed, with a plan before any edits. — id `gh-fix-ci`, score 3.8, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags ci, github-actions, gh-cli, debugging, vendored from https://github.com/openai/skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/gh-fix-ci/entry.yaml)
- [Repository threat model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/security-threat-model/SKILL.md): Write a repository-grounded threat model covering trust boundaries, assets, attacker capabilities, abuse paths, and prioritized mitigations. It checks key assumptions with the user before writing the report, and fires only when asked explicitly. Use when: Someone explicitly asks for a threat model or abuse-path analysis of a codebase or service. — id `security-threat-model`, score 3.8, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags security, threat-modeling, appsec, vendored from https://github.com/openai/skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/security-threat-model/entry.yaml)
- [Systematic debugging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md): Reproduce a failure, test a falsifiable hypothesis about its cause, apply a focused correction, and verify it, with a reference for intermittent and environment-specific failures. Use when: A bug, failing test, crash, or regression needs a diagnosed fix rather than a symptom patch. — id `systematic-debugging`, score 3.8, evidence tested, hosts any, tags debugging, diagnosis, regression, testing, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/systematic-debugging/entry.yaml)
- [Test-driven development (red-green-refactor)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md): Strict red-green-refactor. Write one failing test, watch it fail for the right reason, write the minimum code to pass, and run the whole suite. A companion reference covers tests that name the break they catch and avoid testing mocks. Use when: Projects with a runnable test suite where agents write tests after the fact, write tautological tests, or test mocks instead of behavior. — id `test-driven-development`, score 3.8, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags tdd, testing, discipline, test-quality, vendored from https://github.com/obra/superpowers, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/test-driven-development/entry.yaml)
- [Web app testing with Playwright](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/webapp-testing/SKILL.md): Drive a local web app with Python Playwright, following a reconnaissance-then-action pattern. Includes a helper that starts and stops dev servers around a test script, and examples for element discovery and console logs. Use when: Verifying or debugging frontend behavior headlessly, especially on hosts without a built-in browser. — id `webapp-testing`, score 3.8, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags testing, playwright, frontend, browser, verification, vendored from https://github.com/anthropics/skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/webapp-testing/entry.yaml)
- [MCP server builder](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/b9e19e6f44773509fbdd7001d77ff41a49a486c1/skills/mcp-builder): A four-phase guide for designing, implementing, reviewing, and evaluating MCP servers in Python (FastMCP) or TypeScript, with tool-design best practices and an evaluation harness. Use when: Building or reviewing an MCP server that wraps an external API or service. — id `mcp-builder`, score 3.6, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags mcp, tool-design, api-integration, evaluation, linked from https://github.com/anthropics/skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/mcp-builder/entry.yaml)
- [Find skills on skills.sh](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/tree/773fb2c7bbf16781670a3520affc4abd0c6151ae/skills/find-skills): Search the skills.sh registry with npx skills find, vet candidates by source, install count, and stars, and offer install commands. Use when: You want to search the wider public skills registry, beyond this curated catalog. — id `find-skills`, score 3.0, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags discovery, skills-registry, tooling, linked from https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/find-skills/entry.yaml)
- [Skill creator with evaluations](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/b9e19e6f44773509fbdd7001d77ff41a49a486c1/skills/skill-creator): A complete skill-authoring workflow with test cases, blind comparison, benchmark aggregation, and optimization of a description for trigger accuracy. Use when: Authoring or tuning a skill and measuring whether it triggers and helps; use it as a methodology reference. — id `skill-creator`, score 3.0, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code, tags skill-authoring, evaluation, meta, linked from https://github.com/anthropics/skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/skills/skill-creator/entry.yaml)

## Rules

- [Verify in the running app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/rules/verification-evidence/RULE.md): Check a change where its effect appears, including in an app the user already has running, even when the agent may not start a server; otherwise name what remains unchecked. Use when: Agents in your project hand back visible UI changes without looking at them. — id `verification-evidence`, score 4.0, evidence used, hosts any, tags verification, ui, browser, honesty, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/rules/verification-evidence/entry.yaml)
- [Karpathy-style coding guidelines](https://github.com/multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills/tree/8462496b34419f20b32778610571ac723e91f94c/CLAUDE.md): A widely shared CLAUDE.md with four principles drawn from Andrej Karpathy's observations of LLM coding failures. Surface assumptions, write minimal code, make surgical diffs, and execute toward a goal with verification steps. Use when: You want a recognized, drop-in baseline against over-engineering and drive-by edits. — id `karpathy-coding-guidelines`, score 3.8, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags scope, simplicity, diff-size, assumptions, linked from https://github.com/multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/rules/karpathy-coding-guidelines/entry.yaml)
- [Focused changes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/rules/focused-changes/RULE.md): Make the smallest coherent change that satisfies the request, follow existing project patterns, and avoid unrelated cleanup or new dependencies without a concrete need. Use when: Agents in your project tend to over-reach with refactors, new dependencies, or drive-by cleanup. — id `focused-changes`, score 3.2, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags scope, conventions, diff-size, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/rules/focused-changes/entry.yaml)
- [Scope and authority](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/rules/scope-and-authority/RULE.md): Work toward the requested outcome within the authorization already given, preserve unrelated work, and ask only when the answer changes the result or more authorization is needed. Use when: You want an explicit, host-neutral statement of authorization boundaries in AGENTS.md. — id `scope-and-authority`, score 3.2, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags scope, safety, authorization, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/rules/scope-and-authority/entry.yaml)

## Workflows and loops

- [Self-improvement loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/workflows/self-improvement-loop/WORKFLOW.md): Capture what slowed a session down, place each lesson where it will take effect (hook, always-loaded line, skill, or script), check that it loads, and prune always-loaded instructions regularly. It composes the retrospective, hook, and AGENTS.md entries in this catalog. Use when: You want the agent to learn from each session and write the lessons back into the project without bloating its instructions. — id `self-improvement-loop`, score 4.2, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags self-improvement, retrospective, project-instructions, memory, context-hygiene, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/workflows/self-improvement-loop/entry.yaml)
- [Explore, plan, implement, review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/workflows/explore-plan-implement-review/WORKFLOW.md): Explore read-only and write a plan with a check for each step before editing. Implement against the plan, then have a fresh-context reviewer compare the diff with the plan and report only gaps in correctness or requirements. Use when: A change spans several files, the approach is uncertain, or the agent will run long enough unattended that it should not grade its own work. — id `explore-plan-implement-review`, score 4.0, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags planning, code-review, subagents, verification, adapted from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/workflows/explore-plan-implement-review/entry.yaml)
- [Ralph loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/workflows/ralph-loop/WORKFLOW.md): Fresh-context iteration against a plan. A shell loop reruns one fixed prompt; each pass picks one task from IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, implements it behind tests, commits, and updates the plan, until a completion token or an iteration cap. Use when: You have clear specs and a strong test suite and want long, unattended greenfield or backlog work in a sandbox. — id `ralph-loop`, score 3.4, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags autonomous-loop, long-running, planning, backpressure, adapted from https://ghuntley.com/ralph/, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/workflows/ralph-loop/entry.yaml)
- [Revise CLAUDE.md with session learnings](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/a86e34672c44fa1fb1ae2b2c4143abcf26612ace/plugins/claude-md-management/commands/revise-claude-md.md): An official end-of-session command. It reflects on the context the agent lacked (commands, patterns, gotchas), picks the right CLAUDE.md, drafts one-line additions as diffs with a reason for each, and applies only the ones you approve. Use when: A session showed context the agent was missing, and you want a lightweight, approval-gated write-back to project instructions. — id `revise-claude-md`, score 3.4, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code, tags self-improvement, project-instructions, memory, retrospective, linked from https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/workflows/revise-claude-md/entry.yaml)

## Hooks

- [Format after agent edits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/hooks/format-after-edit/HOOK.md): A PostToolUse hook that runs the project's formatter on files the agent edits, turning a prose style rule into a deterministic step. Includes a Claude Code version keyed on the edited path and a Codex version keyed on changed files. Use when: The project has a formatter, and agents leave style drift or spend turns fixing formatting. — id `format-after-edit`, score 3.8, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code/codex, tags formatting, automation, post-tool-use, adapted from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/hooks/format-after-edit/entry.yaml)
- [Protect files and block destructive commands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/hooks/protect-files-and-commands/HOOK.md): A PreToolUse hook that blocks edits to protected paths (.env, lockfiles, .git/) and recursive force deletes, with a reason the agent can act on. Use when: Agents run with broad edit or auto-approve permissions and you want a cheap extra guardrail against a few known-bad actions. — id `protect-files-and-commands`, score 3.4, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code/codex, tags safety, guardrails, secrets, pre-tool-use, adapted from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/hooks/protect-files-and-commands/entry.yaml)
- [Block "done" until checks pass](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/hooks/stop-gate-checks/HOOK.md): A Stop hook that runs the project's fast typecheck, lint, or tests when the agent tries to finish, and blocks with the failure output until they pass. It has guards against looping and against pure question turns. Use when: Agents end turns with failing checks, or unattended sessions must not finish red. — id `stop-gate-checks`, score 3.4, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code/codex, tags verification, quality-gate, stop-hook, autonomous-loop, adapted from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/hooks/stop-gate-checks/entry.yaml)

## Subagents

- [Silent-failure hunter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/subagents/silent-failure-hunter/AGENT.md): A read-only review subagent that looks only at swallowed errors, broad catches, silent fallbacks, and unhelpful error messages in a diff. Each finding comes with a severity, the failure it hides, and a concrete fix. Use when: A change adds try/catch, fallbacks, retries, or optional chaining, and you want errors surfaced rather than hidden. — id `silent-failure-hunter`, score 4.0, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code/codex, tags code-review, error-handling, reliability, adapted from https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/blob/4ca561fb8532594e7a5faef945e85096fcec0616/plugins/pr-review-toolkit/agents/silent-failure-hunter.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/subagents/silent-failure-hunter/entry.yaml)
- [Code reviewer with confidence filtering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/subagents/pr-review-code-reviewer/AGENT.md): A review subagent that checks the current diff against the project's written rules and for real bugs. It scores each issue from 0 to 100 and reports only those at 80 or above, with the file, line, and a fix. Use when: You want a fresh-context review before commit or PR that enforces your CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md rules while keeping false positives low. — id `pr-review-code-reviewer`, score 3.4, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code, tags code-review, false-positives, project-instructions, quality, vendored from https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/subagents/pr-review-code-reviewer/entry.yaml)

## MCP servers

- [Chrome DevTools MCP](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp): The Chrome team's MCP server, which drives Chrome through DevTools to navigate, click, take screenshots, read the console and network activity, and record performance traces, so agents can verify and debug web changes. Use when: Agents change web UI and need to see the result, read console or network errors, or diagnose performance, especially in Codex or headless setups. — id `chrome-devtools-mcp`, score 4.0, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags browser, verification, debugging, performance, linked from https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/mcps/chrome-devtools-mcp/entry.yaml)
- [Context7 library docs](https://github.com/upstash/context7): Fetches version-specific documentation and code examples for libraries by name, through a remote MCP server or a ctx7 CLI with a skill, so agents stop using outdated APIs. Use when: Agents write code against fast-moving libraries and keep using deprecated or invented APIs. — id `context7`, score 4.0, evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags documentation, libraries, api-accuracy, linked from https://github.com/upstash/context7, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/mcps/context7/entry.yaml)

## Plugins

- [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers): An opinionated end-to-end development method packaged as interlocking skills for brainstorming, planning, subagent execution with review, TDD, debugging, verification, git worktrees, and finishing a branch. It ships manifests for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other hosts. Use when: A team wants a complete, enforced spec-to-merge workflow rather than individual techniques. — id `superpowers`, score 4.4, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code/codex, tags workflow, planning, tdd, subagents, code-review, methodology, linked from https://github.com/obra/superpowers, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/plugins/superpowers/entry.yaml)
- [Compound Engineering](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin): A cross-host plugin of about 36 skills built around brainstorm, plan, work, simplify, review, and compound. Its compound step writes each verified, non-obvious lesson to docs/solutions/, where later planning runs read it. Use when: You want a complete, opinionated plan, review, and learn loop where every change leaves searchable lessons for the next task. — id `compound-engineering`, score 4.0, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code/codex, tags self-improvement, planning, code-review, knowledge-capture, methodology, linked from https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/plugins/compound-engineering/entry.yaml)
- [claude-reflect](https://github.com/BayramAnnakov/claude-reflect): Hooks detect when you correct the agent and queue the correction. /reflect reviews the queue and writes the approved items into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, and /reflect-skills mines session history for repeated tasks to turn into commands. Use when: You keep correcting the agent on the same preferences and want those corrections captured with a review step. — id `claude-reflect`, score 2.6, evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code, tags self-improvement, memory, corrections, project-instructions, linked from https://github.com/BayramAnnakov/claude-reflect, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/entries/plugins/claude-reflect/entry.yaml)

## Collections

- [Debugging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/collections/debugging.yaml): Diagnose and fix defects with a reproduction-first skill and a rule to verify where the change shows up. Entries: systematic-debugging, verification-evidence
- [Project upkeep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/collections/project-upkeep.yaml): Turn session retrospectives into project guidance that loads when needed, together with the verification rule. Entries: retrospective, verification-evidence
- [Self-improvement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/collections/self-improvement.yaml): Learn from each session and write the lessons back where they take effect, while keeping always-loaded instructions short. Entries: self-improvement-loop, retrospective, agents-md-authoring, format-after-edit
- [Starter set](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ban-red/agentic-rules/main/collections/starter.yaml): A small, portable baseline for most software projects. It covers verification before claiming success, hard-bug diagnosis, stress-testing a plan, and lean project instructions. Entries: verification-before-completion, diagnosing-bugs, grilling, agents-md-authoring, verification-evidence
